content: Dr. Odille Chang, affiliated with the School of Medical Sciences at Fiji National University in Suva, Fiji, focuses on capacity-building for mental health in the Western Pacific region. Her work includes the development of a mobile application for screening depression and suicide risk, as well as utilizing art as a tool for recovery. Professor Pamela Collins, from the University of Washington in Seattle, USA, specializes in global public health and mental health research. Her expertise extends to education, training, capacity-building, and leadership in science policy within the Americas region. Professor Pim Cuijpers, based at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam in the Netherlands, is an expert in depression and psychological interventions. His work includes conducting meta-analyses on the efficacy of these interventions and scaling up treatment strategies in Europe. Professor Petrus J. de Vries, from the University of Cape Town in South Africa, focuses on autism spectrum disorders in Africa and low-resource environments. His expertise also includes tuberous sclerosis complex, adolescent health, and health promotion. Dr. Palmira Fortunato dos Santos, affiliated with the Ministry of Health of Mozambique in Maputo, specializes in mental health policy, evaluation, and rehabilitation. She contributes to the implementation of the Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) guidelines for mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in Africa. Professor Chris Dowrick, from the University of Liverpool in the United Kingdom, is an expert in medically unexplained somatic complaints and mental health in primary care. He has contributed to the development of guidelines for depression through the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) in Europe. Dr. Julian Eaton, associated with CBM Global Disability Inclusion in the Netherlands and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom, focuses on mental health in low-income countries and human rights in Europe. Dr. Rabih El Chammay, from the Ministry of Public Health in Lebanon, specializes in public mental health and refugee mental health policy in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Professor Cleusa Ferri, based at the Universidade Federal de São Paulo in Brazil, is an expert in dementia, epidemiology, and care provision for late-life mental disorders in low-resource settings in the Americas. Professor Sandra Fortes, affiliated with the School of Medical Sciences at Rio de Janeiro State University in Brazil, focuses on health policy and medically unexplained symptoms in the Americas. Dr. Michael P. Hengartner, from Zurich University of Applied Sciences in Switzerland, specializes in public mental health, psychiatric epidemiology, social psychiatry, psychopathology, and applied biostatistics in Europe. Dr. Asma Humayun, associated with the Ministry of Planning, Development, and Special Initiatives in Pakistan, works on psychosocial aspects of healthcare in medical training and practice. She is dedicated to scaling up mental health resources and de-stigmatizing mental health care in Pakistan within the Eastern region. Professor Nathalie Jette, from the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York, USA, specializes in adult epilepsy, health services research, and epidemiology in the Americas. Dr. Maria Elena Medina-Mora, affiliated with the Mexican National Autonomous University and the National Institute of Psychiatry in Mexico City, focuses on methodological, psychosocial, and epidemiological issues related to addictions and mental health in the Americas. Professor Pratima Murthy, from the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences in Bengaluru, India, specializes in alcohol and substance use, the history of psychiatry, psychiatry and law, psychiatric training, and neuropsychiatry in South-East Asia. Dr. Dinah Nadera, associated with the Ateneo School of Medicine and Public Health in the Philippines, focuses on research and capacity-building in mental health. Her work includes mental health initiatives for government and civil society organizations in training, research, policy, and legislation in the Western Pacific region. Professor Charles Newton, from the Kenya Medical Research Institute in Kilifi, Kenya, and the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom, specializes in pediatric epilepsy, the epidemiology of epilepsy, and neurodevelopmental disorders in lowand middle-income countries (LMICs) in Africa. Mr. Michael Njenga, affiliated with Users & Survivors of Psychiatry in Kenya and CBM Global Disability Inclusion in the Netherlands, is an expert by experience, a disability rights activist, and a researcher. He contributes to the implementation of the Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) guidelines in Africa. Professor Olayinka Omigbodun, from the University of Ibadan in Nigeria, focuses on child and adolescent mental health, public mental health, and mental health in primary care in Africa. Professor Afarin Rahimi-Movaghar, based at the Iranian National Center for Addiction Studies at Tehran University of Medical Sciences in Iran, specializes in addiction, HIV, and public health in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Professor Atif Rahman, from the University of Liverpool in the United Kingdom, focuses on child and adolescent mental health, global mental health, women’s mental health, psychological interventions for mental disorders in LMICs, and cultural issues in mental health care in Europe. Professor Shekhar Saxena, affiliated with the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in the USA, specializes in the prevention and management of mental, developmental, neurological, and substance use disorders, as well as suicide prevention in the Americas. Ms. Charlene Sunkel, founder and CEO of the Global Mental Health Peer Network in South Africa, is an advocate for lived experience, stigma reduction, and human rights in Africa. Professor Sir Graham Thornicroft, from King’s College London in the United Kingdom, specializes in global mental health, guideline development, mental health services research, and mental health stigma in Europe. Professor Chahnez Triki, from the University of Sfax in Tunisia, focuses on significant emotional and medically unexplained somatic complaints in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Professor Athula Sumathipala, affiliated with the Institute for Research and Development in Sri Lanka and Keele University in the United Kingdom, specializes in psychosis and bipolar disorders in South-East Asia and Europe. Dr. Anish Cherian, from the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences in India, focuses on psychosis and bipolar disorders in South-East Asia. Dr. Adib Essali, associated with Counties Manukau Health and the University of Auckland in New Zealand, specializes in mental health in the Eastern Mediterranean and Western Pacific regions. Professor Oye Gureje, from the University of Ibadan in Nigeria, focuses on severe and enduring mental disorders, service implementation, and clinical trials for the treatment of psychosis and mood disorders in Africa. Dr. Charlotte Hanlon, affiliated with King’s College London in the United Kingdom and Addis Ababa University in Ethiopia, specializes in mental health policy, service planning, and the relationship between poverty and mental health in LMICs in Africa and Europe. Professor Mario Maj, from the University of Naples in Italy, contributes to the Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) guidelines for mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in Europe. Dr. Giovanni Ostuzzi, based at the University of Verona in Italy, focuses on neuroscience, biomedicine, and movement sciences in Europe. Dr. Thara Rangaswamy, from the Schizophrenia Research Foundation in India, specializes in schizophrenia and related disorders in South-East Asia. Ms. Muffy Walker, founder of the International Bipolar Foundation in the USA, focuses on self-harm and suicide in the Americas. Dr. Vladimir Carli, from the Karolinska Institutet in Sweden, specializes in suicide research and prevention in Europe. Professor Jane Pirkis, from the University of Melbourne in Australia, focuses on mental health research and suicide prevention in the Western Pacific region. Dr. Helal Uddin Ahmed, from the National Institute of Mental Health in Bangladesh, specializes in child and adolescent mental health in South-East Asia. Professor Kaarin Anstey, based at the University of New South Wales in Australia, focuses on dementia in the Western Pacific region. Professor Helen Herrman, affiliated with Orygen and the University of Melbourne in Australia, specializes in youth mental health, community mental health, and mental health promotion in the Western Pacific region. Dr. Lola Kola, from the University of Ibadan in Nigeria and the University of Washington in the USA, focuses on global mental health, community mental health, and the integration of mental health into the treatment of chronic noncommunicable diseases in Africa. Professor Crick Lund, affiliated with King’s College London in the United Kingdom and the University of Cape Town in South Africa, specializes in mental health policy, service planning, and the relationship between poverty and mental health in LMICs in Europe and Africa. Professor David Ndetei, from the University of Nairobi in Kenya, focuses on community mental health, early childhood development, and school mental health in Africa. Dr. Alfredo Pemjean, from the Ministry of Health in Chile, specializes in mental health program management in the Americas. Professor Pratap Sharan, from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences in India, focuses on adult psychiatry, public mental health, and global mental health in South-East Asia. Dr. Vandad Sharifi, from Tehran University of Medical Sciences in Iran, specializes in severe and enduring mental disorders, service implementation, and clinical trials for psychosis and mood disorders in the Eastern Mediterranean region.
